content.title: About
content.content: Cake and cupcake are baked goods made from a batter enriched with eggs, sugar, butter and milk. A cake is usually larger, multi‑layered and decorated with frosting, fruit or chocolate, while a cupcake is a single‑serve portion, often flavored with dried fruit, nuts or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cakes originated in ancient Rome where they were called "placenta" and sweetened with honey and cheese.
Modern cupcakes appeared in 19th‑century England as "tea cakes" served with afternoon tea.
The world’s largest cake, baked in 2012 in the USA, weighed over 6 tons.
The classic American Red Velvet cake gets its vivid color from food coloring, not beet juice.
In Japan, “mochi cupcakes” replace wheat flour with glutinous rice flour for a chewy texture.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Cakes and cupcakes provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and dairy in the batter deliver B12, niacin and riboflavin, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Milk products contribute to bone and tooth strength.

items.title: Antioxidants from fruit and berries
items.content: Cakes topped with fresh fruit or berries add vitamin C and polyphenols.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain flour, nuts or dried fruit raises fiber content, supporting digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large portions can raise blood glucose levels and contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Butter‑based cakes contain saturated fats that may affect cholesterol when consumed excessively.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Eggs, milk, nuts and wheat are common allergens that can trigger reactions.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional wheat flour contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cake is typically served in slices, often accompanied by tea or coffee. Cupcakes are convenient as a snack and can be taken on the go. Both can be further decorated with frosting, sprinkles or fresh berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store finished cake in the refrigerator, covered with plastic wrap, for up to 3‑5 days. Cupcakes keep best in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerated for longer storage.
